findings.claim: `relaxedCookieNameRegEx` is deleted, but the parsing code elsewhere in this file almost certainly still references it, leaving a dangling identifier (TS compile error / ReferenceError at runtime).
findings.rationale: The removed comment explicitly stated the strict regex is "used only when producing cookies via serialize(); parsing uses the relaxed regex below", so a parse()/parseSigned() call site consuming `relaxedCookieNameRegEx` is implied. This hunk removes only the declaration; no corresponding call-site update appears in the diff. If the consumer wasn't updated in another hunk, the module fails to compile. The rest of the file isn't shown, so this needs verification, but it is the most likely breakage here.

findings.claim: Dropping the relaxed name regex reverts cookie-name parsing to the strict RFC 6265 token rule, so incoming cookies whose names contain characters like ':' (e.g. "paraglide:lang") will silently be dropped instead of parsed.
findings.rationale: The removed comments document this exact scenario and link honojs/hono#3189. RFC 6265bis section 5.6 directs consumers to be lenient about names other producers emit in the wild; reinstating the producer-side token rule on the consume path is a silent behavior regression for existing callers - cookies simply disappear from the parse result with no error. Confident this is a real behavior change assuming the parse path now falls back to `validCookieNameRegEx`.
